title: Book One · Chapter 158: Who Carries What
story:
Mum is doing paid sewing work. It must be ready before River Street Day. Two shirts and a child's coat are beside her bag. There is a blue skirt too. She has promised them for early in the final week.

Ronan comes in with a carrying list. He waits while she finishes a line of stitches. Then he asks her to read the list.

“The stool, the bag, the picture cover, the map,” she reads. “All under Mum.”

Ronan looks down. He has put his own name beside the little game envelope. He put Mum beside all the large things. Dad may be at work that day.

“That is too much,” she says.

“I can take the cover.”

“And I still have three hands of work.”

“You have two.”

“Exactly.”

They sit at the table. Ronan crosses out his first carrying plan. He starts again on the back of the paper. “What can you carry comfortably?” he asks Mum. She chooses the blue bag with its light books. She cannot carry the stool and all the loose things. Another adult must help with the stool.

“We can make two trips,” Ronan says.

“Perhaps. Ask about Friday at school. Some things can go to school before Saturday afternoon.”

The next morning they ask Miss Wu. Pictures may come on Friday, flat between their boards. She can keep them in the locked classroom. Mum could bring the stool on Saturday morning. She would need another adult to help her. Mr Qiu closes the table at lunch. Then he could walk to school with her. He offers to do that. He can carry the empty pencil box and pad. He cannot carry the heavy stool too. His stock must stay at the gate.

“Can you help us?” Leo asks his mother. She can meet Mum at the green gate on Saturday. They can carry the stool to school together. She will be there at half past one. She has her own errand before that. She cannot come earlier. Ronan writes the exact time beside her name.

He reads the plan to Mum that evening. “Which adult will bring the stool home?” she asks. He has not written that part. They have no name for the return trip yet. They ask the same people about that too. They will need help after four.

They will clear the room. Then Leo's mother can help bring the stool home. Mum agrees to stay for that. The stool has a journey in both directions now. Ronan marks each one on the paper.

Mum looks at the return trips on the list. She asks him to mark each one. Two lines are still empty. He leaves those names blank for now. He takes the list back to Leo and asks. The answer comes the next morning. Ronan writes the answer down at once. Now Leo's mother has agreed to help after four. They have a plan for the end of the afternoon.

“How will you bring your pictures?” he also asks Mei. Her mother will bring them on Friday after school. Mei wants to open the cover herself. Ronan writes that down. He does not add her pictures to his own pile.

At home Mum works until the light grows soft. Ronan sorts the loose game cards beside her. The cloth and the paper make different little sounds. He looks at the lines Mum has sewn. There are only a few more to do.

“Thank you for asking before Saturday,” she says.

He looks at the first list, with everything under her name. He turns it over, leaving the new plan on top. Several people have agreed to help now. Mum has fewer things to carry. Ronan leaves the new list on the table. Mum can see it there.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：comfortably＝轻松合适地；both directions＝来回两个方向；errand＝外出办的小事。

情节提示：stitches＝针脚；envelope＝信封；paid＝有报酬的。

理解：1. 最初的搬运清单有什么问题？2. 大家怎样安排了凳子的来回搬运？
